correctness.rationale: There are V_i V_j eligible cross edges with rate 1/n each. For X_n=V/n this gives density rates n x_i x_j and increments −(e_i+e_j)/n, with fluid solution u(t)1, u=(1+2t)^{-1}. The scaled martingale has jumps O(n^{-1/2}) and its bracket converges uniformly on bounded intervals to the integral of B(u1). To check the needed moment bound, its optional squared-jump sum is at most 2/n times the total attempt count, a Poisson variable of mean 3nT; this bounds the second moment of the optional quadratic variation. The martingale maximal inequality and Lipschitz Gronwall bound then give bounded fourth moments of the fluctuation supremum. Thus drift Taylor remainders vanish in the path CLT and fluctuation products are uniformly integrable, which is necessary for the actual covariance limit. The linear drift and bracket matrices are −u(I+11ᵀ) and u²(I+11ᵀ); integrating the common and contrast variance equations gives 2(u−u⁴)/3 and u log(1+2t)/2, with zero initial data. Their difference divided by three is the cross-part covariance. Its numerator H(y)=4(1−y^{-3})−3 log y, y=1+2t, starts at zero, increases to y=4^{1/3}, then decreases to −∞. Independent replay: python /workspace/independent_checks.py (adsorption routine) obtains 1.347345267068252110 from the principal Lambert W root in z=y^{-3}, the other real branch giving t=0. This is a fixed-finite-time limiting transition; moment convergence establishes matching finite-n signs at each fixed interior nonzero point, not a universal finite-size transition or a jamming statement. value.rationale: The result gives a structural difference between total vacancy fluctuations and class-imbalance fluctuations, leading to an exact sign reversal under the same irreversible deposition law. Neither the known fluid law nor terminal matching efficiency can predict this transient covariance. The sign classification also predicts signs of large finite systems at fixed times away from the zeros without overclaiming a universal finite-size threshold.
